Off that rig there is no window, every Paint returns a typed refusal and every proof string is empty - so a comparison keyed to the machine property would be two empty strings agreeing with each other about a surface that was never created, which is precisely the vacuity this list exists to prevent. skipSemantics: May-skip, not must-skip: a listed test that runs and passes on a machine where its precondition holds is green. Matching is exact on the pre-'(' portion of the TRX result testName (xunit theory rows serialize with arguments, e.g. Class.Method(x: 1)); a name with no parens matches whole. Anchor is the TRX result list, never Counters arithmetic.
admissionRule: allowedSkips is not a quarantine list. A test may be listed only when its precondition is a property of the machine or OS that cannot be satisfied by configuration during a contract run, and its change names the machine class where it executes. Two named PERMANENT BANS apply: (1) CcpClient.Tests.DataRootOverrideTests.DefaultSettingsPath_EnvUnset_IsThePlatformDefault must never be allowed to skip because a process-wide CCP_DATA_ROOT override makes the floor vacuous; (2) CcpClient.Tests.ChaosTunnelLoopbackTests.Logging_RouteClassesOnly_NeverFilenameOrQuery must be fixed at the source, never quarantined.
bumpRule: Bump total only in the same commit as the test change that moves the count, with the reason recorded here. Never widen, disable, or special-case a check to make a step pass. Adding a name to allowedSkips requires the admission rule above and the machine class where it executes.
lastMovedBy: +14 unit, headless unchanged at 280: THE PER-FRAME COST WAS MEASURED AND MY PREMISE DID NOT SURVIVE IT. I briefed this lane that the full-surface verification read-back was the cost. A per-stage probe on the running product splits a 141 ms spiral frame: GDI+ DrawImageRectRect at HighQualityBicubic is 130 ms (92%), GIF SelectActiveFrame 5.9 ms, and ConfirmContent - the read-back the brief blamed - is 4.6 ms, THREE POINT THREE PERCENT. Confirmed by a second probe: deleting ConfirmContent ENTIRELY moves the spiral from 4.65/4.91 Hz to 5.06 Hz, inside twice the run-to-run spread. The board's '62 MB of pixel traffic per frame' was arithmetically right about the bytes and wrong about the time - GDI moves 20 MB in 2.2 ms, about 9 GB/s, while GDI+ resamples one frame in 130 ms. THE REAL ANSWER CAME FROM THE MEASUREMENT ITSELF: SpiralFrameSource used HighQualityBicubic, WHICH UPSTREAM USES NOWHERE. WPF resamples a spiral frame at exactly one place, with HighQualityBilinear, caching at a 1280 cap and letting the compositor stretch. Plain Bilinear was measured and is WORSE (1.8 Hz), so the choice is upstream's named filter rather than the cheapest one. Picture cost measured rather than asserted: mean absolute difference 0.45 and 0.84 of 255 per channel, max 33, with 0.09% and 0.45% of channels off by more than 8. THE BANDED CHECK SHIPPED ANYWAY, AT ITS HONEST SIZE: Paint still blits, still asks the OS for the content back and still compares it on EVERY frame - only the REGION changed. The whole surface after any event that could have changed the WINDOW (Present, SetClickThrough, resize, a Reassert of the band, or a failed comparison), one sweeping band of 16 otherwise, so every row is re-read within 16 frames, one-shot surfaces are unchanged, and a surface that stops holding its frame is still detected and still withdrawn. The bounded re-proof rides the caller's existing cadence - no new timer. BEFORE AND AFTER, ONE BINARY PER SIDE, ONE HARNESS, TWO SAMPLES EACH. Spiral alone: 4.65 and 4.91 Hz to 6.30 and 6.27 Hz (+31%), CPU 66.1/65.4 to 56.6/56.8 percent of one core, UI loop p50 105/100 ms to 56/57 ms; noise floor before was +/-5.4% and after +/-0.5%, so the win is about six times the floor. All modules at maximum, 15-16 native surfaces: aggregate surface change rate 11.97/12.50 Hz to 14.90/17.39 Hz with the after-MINIMUM above the before-maximum, UI loop p90 1230/1365 ms to 860/804 ms (-35%), max 1472/1634 to 1106/1079 (-30%). CPU stayed at ~95% of one core AND THAT IS EXPECTED - the thread is still saturated, it just delivers more frames. INSTRUMENT HONESTY: the harness's own probe costs 37-39% of a core and a control run with it off is included. THE HEADLINE IS NOT A FIX: intended is 33-50 Hz and the spiral reaches 6.3, still a 5-8x shortfall; at maximum the UI thread still stalls for 0.8-1.1 s. Measurably better, not fixed. TWO SITES MEASURED AND DELIBERATELY LEFT: the pointer/bubble path costs 42.7-47.9% of one core alone, and its per-move read-back splits into z-order walk 0.07 ms, hit test 0.09 ms and INK READ 7.6 ms - so my brief was wrong there too, the ~400 GetPixel are 98% of it and the z-order walk I named is 0.6%. Untouched because the overlay's rule does not transfer: a bubble MOVES every 30 ms, so 'the position did not change' is false for every frame and only the ink read can come off the per-move path. That is the next lane's biggest lever. And one thread for seven presenters is why CPU sits at 95% of ONE core with fifteen idle - an architecture decision, not a packet.
